title: Shell suites grade with `printf ... | grep -q` under pipefail: two unrelated suites failed a loaded preflight with "printf: write error: Broken pipe" (150 such lines in 29 files)
description:
## BLUF

Two unrelated shell suites each failed once inside preflight leg 14 of a pre-push, on the same tell, `printf: write error: Broken pipe`, while the machine was heavily loaded. Both grade a result with `printf '%s' "$out" | grep -qF ...` under `set -uo pipefail`. Both passed every time on a quiet machine (15 of 15 runs). **The failure was NOT reproduced under load, so the mechanism below is the explanation that fits, not a proven one.** The same line shape appears at 150 places in 29 files.

## What was seen

Two pushes ran their pre-push hook at the same time on one macOS laptop (12 CPUs). A Docker Desktop VM was at about 920% CPU and the load average read 98 / 100 / 98 at 00:45Z and my later readings of the 1-minute figure were 74 (00:52Z), 58 (01:12Z), 39 (01:13Z) and 6.65 (01:18Z), after Docker Desktop was restarted. Leg 14 took 947 s and 1007 s; the same leg took 553 s on an unloaded run earlier. Each push was a branch off develop `28dac5c12ba5` carrying a two-file change that touches neither suite. Both pushes were refused, `PREFLIGHT FAILED on leg(s) 14 - (13/16 legs ran)`, every other leg passing.

`check_shared_relink.test.sh` (push started 00:47:52Z, `shell suites: 90 passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped (of 92)`):

```
.../scripts/__tests__/check_shared_relink.test.sh: line 49: printf: write error: Broken pipe
  FAIL: F-6 inv: distroless nodejs is DENIED (exit correct, WRONG rule fired — wanted /a JavaScript runtime/)
        ::error::./services/thing/Dockerfile — re-link invariant (KS-921): final stage writes node_modules nowhere — but its base image is `gcr.io/distroless/nodejs22-debian12`, a JavaScript runtime, ...
  111 passed, 1 failed, 0 skipped
```

The captured output printed under the FAIL line contains the wanted text, so the rule fired and the grade was wrong. Line 49 is `if [ -n "$want_out" ] && ! printf '%s' "$out" | grep -qF -- "$want_out"; then`.

`ks1355_slot_blind_launchers.test.sh` (push started 00:49:30Z, `shell suites: 89 passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped (of 91)`):

```
.../scripts/__tests__/ks1355_slot_blind_launchers.test.sh: line 68: printf: write error: Broken pipe
FAIL CONTROL no slot named: the banner shows the historic 6882 and 6881
       want "yes yes"
        got "no yes"
ks1355_slot_blind_launchers: 22 passed, 1 failed
```

Line 68 is the helper `saw() { if printf '%s' "$2" | grep -qF -- "$1"; then echo yes; else echo no; fi; }`.

## Measured on a quiet machine

* `check_shared_relink.test.sh`, 10 consecutive runs, hermetic env (`env -i HOME PATH`), load about 4.5, tree `6bb63146affd` (develop `28dac5c12ba5` plus one two-file branch): **10 of 10 passed, 112 passed / 0 failed, 0 "Broken pipe".**
* `ks1355_slot_blind_launchers.test.sh`, 5 consecutive runs, same env, load 3.5 to 4.9, tree `b5767aa4c527` (tree identical to develop `28dac5c12ba5`): **5 of 5 passed, 23 passed / 0 failed, 0 "Broken pipe".**

## Not measured

The failure was not reproduced under load: no deliberate stress was run (it would have disturbed live pushes), so there is no measured failure rate under load. Only two failures were seen, one per suite, in one window. The mechanism is inferred from the shape: `grep -q` exits at its first match, a `printf` still writing to that pipe gets EPIPE, and `pipefail` turns the pipeline's status into failure, so a MATCH is graded as no match. It is a race between two processes, which fits "only when the machine is slow".

## The census, and its frame

`git grep -n -E 'printf [^|]*\| *grep -q'` at commit `28dac5c12ba5c00d9fc3ad04daee5230eff71619`, pathspecs `Blockchain/Dev/scripts` and `systemTest`, excluding `node_modules`: **150 lines in 29 files** (22 under `__tests__`, 7 product scripts); 26 of the 29 files mention `pipefail`. `check_shared_relink.test.sh` holds 13 of the lines, `ks1355_slot_blind_launchers.test.sh` 1. Not counted: 12 `echo ... | grep -q` lines (the sibling shape); other pipe-to-early-exit-reader shapes (`| head`, `| grep -m1`); any directory outside the two pathspecs. The count says nothing about which of the 150 can actually be hit: it is the number of lines with the shape.

## Siblings

* KS-1716 (In Progress): the same defect class in one script, `systemTest/scripts/check-package-format.sh`, where the large-input case silently dropped a package. Not these suites.
* KS-1149 (Backlog, archived): a different cause of a similar-looking push failure (`rc 141` after the gate PASSED; GitHub closes the idle ssh session). Not this one: here the hook itself refuses with `PREFLIGHT FAILED on leg(s) 14`.

## Searched before filing (board, title and description, archived included)

`check_shared_relink` (KS-956, KS-948, KS-937: the guard itself, not this flake); `ks1355_slot_blind_launchers` (KS-1558: gate follow-ups); `write error: Broken pipe` and `Broken pipe` (KS-1716 only); `grep -q` (KS-1716, KS-1624, KS-1134, KS-998, KS-912, KS-469); `pipefail` (8 hits, none about these suites); `EPIPE` (KS-1716, KS-1598); `SIGPIPE` (KS-1716, KS-1583, KS-1149). The terms `Broken pipe`, `EPIPE` and `SIGPIPE` all find KS-1716, so the search can see this class. No open ticket names either suite as flaking.

## Update 2026-10-26 02:20Z: a third suite, at moderate load, and a measurement that weakens the first explanation

**Third occurrence.** A third push was refused at leg 14 with the same tell. Push of the KS-1513 branch, started 01:53:06Z, ended `rc 1` after 1081 s: `shell suites: 90 passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped (of 92)`, FAILED `preflight_deps.test.sh`, which printed

```
.../scripts/__tests__/preflight_deps.test.sh: line 443: printf: write error: Broken pipe
.../scripts/__tests__/preflight_deps.test.sh: line 444: printf: write error: Broken pipe
FAIL KS-1638: that refusal SHORT-CIRCUITS — a red suite present, still not run
       want "HOOKCTL-REFUSED/1", got "OTHER/1"
preflight_deps: 60 passed, 1 failed
```

Lines 443 and 444 are consecutive `elif printf '%s' "$out" | grep -q '...'` verdict tests; in this cell the text for 443 (`could not derive the pre-push hook's own control`) sits at byte 1871 and the text for 444 (`de-slotted`) at byte 1821 of `$out`, so both match early and both pipelines failed, which sent the cell to the `OTHER` verdict. **This one was NOT in the 60 to 98 load window:** leg 14 took 662 s (against 553 s unloaded), and my readings of the 1-minute load average over the push were between 4.0 and 13.

**Quiet-box runs of this suite:** 6 of 6 passed on that exact tree (`716e26290155`, 61 passed / 0 failed, 0 "Broken pipe"), load about 6.

**What the measurement does to the explanation.** Using the suite's own `PREFLIGHT_FIXTURE_OUT` capture on the failing cell, `$out` is **2848 bytes**, 62 lines. That is far below the macOS pipe buffer (`st_blksize` 16384), so a single `write()` of it cannot meet a closed reader. The "large output, early match" form of the race is therefore NOT what happened here; for it to occur, bash 3.2's `printf` would have to deliver the string to `grep` in several small writes. I tried to reproduce that on the real captured output: 3 runs of 3000 iterations of `set -uo pipefail; printf '%s' "$out" | grep -q "could not derive the pre-push hook's own control"`, load about 8 to 10, **0 of 9000 reported no-match.** Not reproduced.

**Tally of pushes of mine that reached leg 14 since 00:43Z:** 6; refused by this tell: 3 (the KS-1391 and KS-1560 first attempts, and the KS-1513 push above); passed: 3 (the KS-1560 and KS-1391 second attempts, and KS-1289). A seventh push, KS-1716, ran no preflight leg. The refused ones were three different suites. So the suites are sometimes fragile on this machine under contention from several simultaneous preflights; the mechanism is unproven.

nodes.title: Refs KS-1728: batch 2: 33 negative sites lose the temp file, 12 product lines lose the early-closing pipe, an empty pattern is refused (a form change, not a proven cure)
Refs KS-1728: seven shell suites grade 101 lines without a pipe (batch 1): a form change on 108 sites, not a proven cure
test(shell): grade four printf|grep -q lines without a pipe (KS-1728, the four observed lines)

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Batch 2 is delivered as PR 2074 (shell only, tier 1 asked, head e8c950ecb30d, base develop d00221c38e12): https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/2074. It waits for its QA gate and is not merged or deployed. It is a form change, not a proven cure: the flake was never reproduced under load.

**What it holds.** 33 negative-shape sites in five suites read `[[ "$v" == *'literal'* ]]` instead of a here-string grep (gate 228 F1: a failed temp file read as "no match"). 12 lines in seven product scripts read `printf ... | grep PAT >/dev/null` instead of `... | grep -q PAT` (gate 226 Q9); scripts 1, 3 and 4 have no pipefail, so their cells pin the form only. `b_arm_case` refuses an empty expected substring (gate 228 F2). One new 29-cell suite pins the 12 lines. `preflight.sh` is not in the batch: another change holds it.

**Measured.** The seven suites report the same cells before and after (36, 18, 112 to 114 with the two new F2 cells, 32, 10, 16, 82). Always-match turns 31 of the 33 sites red, never-match none, 2 crash arms unreachable on a green run. The fault `( trap '' XFSZ; ulimit -f 0; ... )` silences one red cell per site on develop for 10 hook sites and none on this branch. The new suite is red on develop (19 failed) and its 12 line mutants each turn exactly two cells red.

**Not run:** the four platform suites, a natural temp-write failure (the fault is injected), any shell other than bash 3.2.57, shellcheck, a load experiment, any LTS Node (v26.8.1 only, not involved). F1 was driven on 10 of the 31 reachable sites.

**Remainder list:** the update to comment 8bb0bb2d (new sha, commands named, new counts) waits until the gate has read it.

**Pre-push hook:** PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 13/16 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed. |   legs 3 4 8 — local stack not up; you can clear this by starting it. |   This is NOT a pass. Do not quote it as one — say which legs ran.

**BLUF:** Batch 1 is delivered as PR 2047 (test-only, tier 2, head 0dbf24bc0ce4, base develop aa4200e8a34c): https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/2047. It waits for its QA gate and is not merged. 101 lines holding 108 sites in seven shell suites now read grep -q ... <<<"$out" instead of printf | grep -q. **A form change, not a proven cure:** the failure was never reproduced under load and the threshold is not bracketed. The census falls from 154 lines in 31 files to 53 in 24. This ticket stays open with the remainder below.

**Measured.** The seven suites report the same cells before and after (36, 18, 112, 32, 10, 16 and 82 pass; 0 failed; 0 "Broken pipe"). Planted corruptions, one site at a time, file restored by sha256: 104 of 108 sites turn the suite red (73 by a never-matching pattern, 31 by an always-matching one); seven no-op controls stay green. Four sites no corruption reaches on a green run: orchestrate_jobs lines 208 and 448 (diagnostic text, evaluated only after a cell failed) and run_shell_suites lines 166 and 201 (CRASHED arms of two classifiers). Every site was read whole; no pattern can match an empty line, so no verdict can move. Each rewrite is proved by a round trip, 101 of 101.

**Remainder (53 lines in 24 files, at the PR's tree).** 8 product scripts (15 lines) are a question before an edit because they run on developers' pushes; 16 test files (38 lines) are next-batch candidates, with ks1347 named by KS 1560 and the systemTest files in another lane.

- 1  scripts/__tests__/check_stack_safety_hook_env.test.sh

**Not run:** a load experiment, any shell other than bash 3.2.57, shellcheck (not installed), the four platform suites.
